card.headline: Another word for where
card.sub: whereabouts · which part of · which way · in which · wherever

beats.role: answer on screen at 0:00 (H104) + open loop (closed in the 'where ... in' tip). Phrase said inside a context sentence so 'where' cannot be heard as 'wear' / 'were' (critic note on the 'and'/'end' hook).
beats.speech: Another word for where, as in: where do you live? Whereabouts, which part of, which way, in which, and wherever. Ten words in all. And stay for the little word that many learners add at the end by mistake.

card.headline: Plain:  This report looks at the areas where crime is rising and where it is falling.
card.sub: Report style:  This report looks at the areas in which crime is rising and those in which it is falling.

beats.role: before/after beat. Labelled Plain -> Report style, NO cross: both sentences are correct (critic fix 1 on h104-how, 0:14 card).
beats.speech: Plain English: this report looks at the areas where crime is rising, and where it is falling. Report style: this report looks at the areas in which crime is rising, and those in which it is falling. Both are correct. The second one just sounds more formal, like a real report.

card.headline: Where are you?  ·  Where is my phone?
card.sub: Keep where here. Swap it to ask about direction or part of a place, or after a noun.

beats.speech: But not every where can be swapped. Where are you? Where is my phone? In questions like these, keep where. Swap it when you ask for a direction or a part of a place, or when it comes after a noun.

beats.label: where in questions
beats.chapter: Another word for where in questions
beats.speech: Part one. Five ways to ask where.

card.headline: Whereabouts
card.meaning: where, roughly, in what area (informal, mostly British)
card.example: Whereabouts in London do you live?

beats.speech: Whereabouts. It means where, roughly, in what area. It's informal and mostly British. Whereabouts in London do you live?

card.headline: Which part of
card.meaning: where in a city or a country (everyday)
card.example: Which part of Spain are you from?

beats.speech: Which part of. Use it when you want more than the country or the city. Which part of Spain are you from?
Which way. It asks for the direction. Which way is the station?

card.headline: How do I get to
card.meaning: where is, when you need directions (everyday, polite)
card.example: Excuse me, how do I get to the city centre?

beats.speech: How do I get to. Ask this instead of where is, when you need directions. Excuse me, how do I get to the city centre?

card.headline: What's the address
card.example: What's the address of the hotel?

beats.speech: What's the address. It asks where exactly, down to the street. What's the address of the hotel?

card.headline: Do you know where is the station?  ✗
card.sub: Do you know where the station is?  ✓   ·   Which way is the station?  ✓

beats.role: common mistake / contrast pair (real error: question word order inside an indirect question)
beats.speech: Careful. Don't say: do you know where is the station? Say: do you know where the station is? Or just: which way is the station?

card.headline: Which one fits?
card.question: Excuse me, ___ is the beach?
card.answer: Excuse me, which way is the beach?

beats.speech: Which one fits? Excuse me. Blank. Is the beach? Which way, or which part of? | Which way. It asks for the direction.

card.headline: Which one fits?
card.question: ___ town do you live in?
card.options: Which part of / How do I get to
card.answer: Which part of town do you live in?
card.note: which part of = where in a place

beats.speech: Which one fits? Blank. Town do you live in? Which part of, or how do I get to? | Which part of. Which part of town do you live in?

card.headline: Say it now
card.sentences:
Whereabouts do you live?
Which way is the station?
Which part of town are you in?

beats.speech: Now say it with me. Listen, then repeat. | Whereabouts do you live? | Which way is the station? | Which part of town are you in?

beats.label: where inside a sentence
beats.chapter: Another word for where in sentences
beats.speech: Part two. Five words for where inside a sentence.

card.headline: In which
card.example: We found a quiet room in which nobody could hear us.

beats.speech: In which. Use it after a noun, instead of where. It's formal, so keep it for writing. We found a quiet room in which nobody could hear us.

card.headline: That ... in
card.meaning: where, with in at the end (everyday)
card.example: This is the town that I grew up in.

beats.speech: That, with in at the end. Everyday English often says: This is the town that I grew up in. You can even drop that: the town I grew up in.

card.headline: Wherever
card.meaning: in any place, it doesn't matter where (neutral)

beats.speech: Wherever. It means in any place, it doesn't matter where. Sit wherever you like.

card.headline: The location of
card.example: Send me the location of the restaurant.

beats.speech: The location of. It means where something is. Send me the location of the restaurant.
If possible. Instead of where possible, you can say if possible. Use public transport if possible.

card.headline: This is the town where I grew up in.  ✗
card.sub: the town where I grew up  ✓   ·   the town I grew up in  ✓

beats.role: open loop closed (hook) / common mistake (real error: where + stranded in)
beats.speech: And here is the little word from the start. Not: this is the town where I grew up in. Say: the town where I grew up. Or: the town I grew up in. Where, or in at the end, never both.

card.headline: In which with friends?
card.sub: With friends: the town I grew up in  ·  In a report: the town in which

beats.speech: Can you say in which to a friend? You can, but it sounds stiff. With friends, say: the town I grew up in.

card.headline: Which one fits?
card.question: This is the house ___ I was born.
card.answer: This is the house in which I was born.
card.note: which alone needs in: the house which I was born in

beats.speech: Which one fits? This is the house. Blank. I was born. In which, or which? | In which. This is the house in which I was born.

card.headline: Which one fits?
card.question: You can park ___ you want.
card.answer: You can park wherever you want.

beats.speech: Which one fits? You can park. Blank. You want. Wherever, or the location of? | Wherever. It means in any place you want.
